Q: Python and Windows: Where is the Python launcher? A:

Adding python to the environment variables in Windows will make the python executable itself global and can be used anywhere.

The primary purpose of the Py launcher (py.exe and pyw.exe) is you can launch a specific version of python py -3.14 temp.py or py -3.13 temp.py The second is the shebang in the head of your scripts...

# temp.py

#!C:\Program Files\Python313\python.exe

import sys

print(sys.version)

3.13.11 (tags/v3.13.11:6278944, Dec 5 2025, 16:26:58) [MSC v.1944 64 bit (AMD64)]

# temp.py

#!C:\Program Files\Python314\python.exe

import sys

print(sys.version)

3.14.2 (tags/v3.14.2:df79316, Dec 5 2025, 17:18:21) [MSC v.1944 64 bit (AMD64)]

so you can simply type the filename into the console temp.py and press enter and the py launcher will map it to the right executable to run the script.

Also, .py and .pyw files are associated to py.exe and pyw.exe.

To keep it simple and use different versions of python in the console; copy the python.exe and past it into the same folder and rename it to python3.13.exe and python3.14.exe so you can use these in the console python3.13 temp.py and python3.14 temp.py.

Last...

If you install python for the current user %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python314 you wont have any issues installing packages with pip.

If you install Python for all users you'll need to make sure you load the console with Run as administrator so when you install packages with pip the packages end up where they should be; inside the the folder where Python was installed C:\Program Files\Python314 or they'll end up in %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Roaming\Python\Python314

Q: How can I best optimize a Bigquery SQL by appending completely redundant filters to the query? A:

Execution time doesn't matter - compare slot-time. You might have problem with resources allocation - you can look into creating reservations to accommodate them: https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reservations-tasks.

Another thing is:

ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( PARTITION BY TIME ORDER BY TIME DESC ) = 1

what do you mean by this, it just returns first processed record for each unique TIME (since you partition by TIME - order doesn't matter it's all the same TIME). Windowing functions are always heavy - if you have a key identifying row accuracy within same TIME - it would be better if you isolate it to sep CTE.

Q: Mercurial hg ignore does not work properly A:

For what it's worth, I think changes in the ignore file should be reflected after the fact by a smart system. I don't remember exactly but git might be doing the proper thing, since it has a staging area. But let's say you added files, but forgot to update .hgignore. Here is what I did: hg forget *, hg addremove. I don't need to manually try to track down which included files should not have been. And in fact there should be a command to list, or a warning about tracked files that are currently ignored. My two cents.

Q: Why is my JavaScript querySelectorAll not selecting elements by ID? A:

You need to understand the difference between the following concepts:

  • Classes and IDs
  • Selecting via document.getElementById
  • Selecting via document.querySelectorAll

As others already have mentioned, IDs have to be unique on your page. You can read more about why here.

In short: Selecting via ID will always return ONE element, no matter if you use getElementById or querySelectorAll. What might be confusing is, that CSS does not care and will always apply the style to all elements with the same ID. You can check the following snippet and play around with the concept:

https://jsfiddle.net/wt6sna8c/2/

Classes however can be reused however often you want.

You can read more about when to use classes and when to use IDs here.

Classes are always selected with a prefix of .. Meaning if you want to select an element with the class "myclass" you would need .myclass as the CSS selector. IDs on the other hand are selected with the prefix #. In your example the selector for ONE element with the id="ss" would be #ss.

These CSS selectors are also used in JavaScript code. The function, that you use, document.querySelectorAll("..."); takes a CSS selector as an argument and returns all matching elements. However, as mentioned, since IDs have to be unique it will always return 0-1 elements if you select via ID, even if you use the function selectorAll.

To fix your code just replace the assignment of id="ss" to class="ss" and use the correct selector prefix in your JS. Here is how that would look like:

https://jsfiddle.net/ma2v1h4n/1

I advise you to play around with selectors and read up on it a bit yourself so you properly understand the concept.

Edit:

As @trincot correctly mentioned your current code actually looks for <ss> tags. Maybe, with that information, you could tell me how you could make the code run as expected without using classes or ids?

Q: Draw a focus frame around a custom widget A:

(5 years pass and we all grow a little older)

Here's an answer that works for GTK4. Weirdly, all you have to do is add the following line of code to your class_init method:

gtk_widget_class_set_css_name (widget_class, I_ ("checkbutton"));

This works because (in most if not all themes, AFAICT), checkbutton includes a suitable CSS selector for :focus, so you get the same colour focus rectangle for your custom widget as for a checkbutton. This, in my case certainly, is what you want.

Please note that gtk_render_focus() is deprecated in GTK4 and, as the OP points out, doesn't work very well anyway.

Note also that the focus rectangle only shows when you tab to the widget, and even then only momentarily. Like it or loathe it, GTK's built-in widgets behave in the same way.

Q: html-validate class-pattern: How to allow Tailwind CSS syntax while enforcing kebab-case? A:

NOTE: But I think this is too much fuss over nothing. Ultimately, if you enter an invalid Tailwind CSS class, it simply won't work.

So the question is related to an npm package, and from your configuration only this part is relevant:

{
  "rules": {
    "class-pattern": [
      "error",
      {
        "pattern": "kebabcase"
      }
    ]
  }
}

The documentation for the mentioned class-pattern rule:

  • Require a specific class format
  • Predefined patterns

From the test files it is clear that it accepts regex, and even multiple rules/regexes/combinations in string[] format as well.

The regex for matching Tailwind CSS classes:

^([a-zA-Z0-9-]+:)*-?[a-zA-Z0-9-]*-([a-zA-Z0-9]+|\d+(\.\d+)?|\[[^\]]+\]|\(--[^\)]+\))?(\/([a-zA-Z0-9]+|\d+(\.\d+)?|\[[^\]]+\]|\(--[^\)]+\)))?!?$
  • Tests

I didn't go overboard, but the general syntax is:

  • texts, numbers, and hyphens can appear as variants
  • variants are joined with :
  • texts, numbers, and hyphens are allowed in the class name
  • in the class name, after the last hyphen, [] usage is allowed, containing almost any text
  • in the class name, after the last hyphen, () usage is allowed, containing a CSS variable
  • after the value in the class name, a / is allowed, followed by another value
  • an optional ! is allowed at the very end of the class name

It seems that in the case of predefined rules, the developers did not consider Tailwind CSS users. This would be worth opening an issue for, suggesting - via a regex - that it would be useful to make it available under the name "tailwindcss".

Q: Why does the Tkinter canvas-leave event behave differently in Windows 11 and Linux Mint? A:

I'm under windows 11 and have the exact same behavior as you stated under linux mint. Which is logical

-> `<Enter-Frame>`-> `<Leave-Frame>` -> `<Leave-Canvas>`-> `<Leave-Window>`
-> `<Enter-Window>` -> `<Enter-Canvas>`

That been said, it's entirely up to the window manager of the OS to post such Events, tkinter does not generate them, tkinter respond to the events.

How can I avoid such problems?

It's not clear what you try to accomplish. Generally speaking, it's a sign of bad code if you over and over bind and unbind events. Extract the important information of the event and handle it the way you want.
